subject: Post-demo: NovaCorp ML Assist - prompt & edge-case capture, model suggestions
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia@novacorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: NovaCorp ML Assist - prompt & edge-case capture, model suggestions

Hi Olivia — great to meet the NovaCorp team earlier. Quick recap + clear next steps so we stay aligned.

What we covered (brief):
- Demo of the ML Assist prototype (context window ~2k tokens, rapid-turn conversation, structured output templates)
- Primary objectives you shared: high precision on legal clause extraction, safe_redaction for PII, and low-latency inline suggestions for end users.
- Risk/constraints: sample size limited today, some existing prompts include raw PHI.

What we need from you to run a targeted model-fit eval: 
1) Prompt samples (CSV) — 50–150 representative prompts across-devices, prioritized by frequency. Include a short "expected_output" column or at least examples of acceptable answers.
2) Edge cases you care about (10–20 examples) — e.g., obfuscated PHI, merged clauses, non-English snippets.
3) Redaction guidance — rules or a short list of PII types to remove or token-replace. If you can’t share raw PHI, please replace values with [REDACTED] and annotate the type (SSN/email/etc).

Recommended plan from Redwood for the eval: 
- We’ll run model-fit tests on 3 variants: a high-accuracy model (Llama-2-Chat-13B q4_0), a latency/throughput-optimized option (rw-opt-7b-int8), and a conservative safety-tuned variant (rw-safety-7b). We’ll provide token/latency cost estimates and a short benchmark report.
- Deliverables: 1) bench report (accuracy/latency/cost), 2) a short prompt-refactor checklist, 3) suggested quantization and batching profile.

Files: I’ve attached a sample prompt CSV template (novacorp_prompt_samples.csv) with headers we prefer; you can use it as-is or export from your tracker.

Asks: Could you share an initial batch by EOD Friday (7/31)? If you need extra privacy assurances, we can set up a VPC/private ingest for the samples — happy to have our security engineer join that conversation.

Thanks — I’ll block 30 minutes next week for a quick handoff once you upload the prompts.

—
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132
Redwood Inference

From: Olivia Barnes <olivia@novacorp.com>

Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 17:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: NovaCorp ML Assist - prompt & edge-case capture, model suggestions

Thanks, Soojin — really helpful recap. I appreciate the template. A few notes from our side: 

- We can export ~120 real prompts from our product logs, but they include user-entered names/emails. We'll sanitize and replace values with [REDACTED] per your guidance.
- Edge cases: merged-officer-names, abbreviated dates ("03/24/21" vs "Mar 24, 2021"), non-English (small percentage Spanish/Portuguese), and documents with OCR errors.
- Compliance: we need confirmation that sample data won’t be used for training and will be deleted after the eval. Can you confirm retention and non-training policy?

Also attaching two sample rows to this reply (inline) to show the fields we can export. I’ll upload a sanitized CSV to the Drive folder you shared by Thursday EOD.

Quick ask: can you tell us which of your recommended models you expect will meet a 0.92 F1 threshold on clause extraction for our initial seed? That will help prioritize which configs we validate first.

Best,
Olivia
Head of Product, NovaCorp

Attachment: (inline sample rows)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia@novacorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 09:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: NovaCorp ML Assist - prompt & edge-case capture, model suggestions

Hi Olivia — thanks for the quick reply and for confirming the export plan. Short answers up front: 

- Data handling: Redwood will not use your uploaded samples to train public models; we can enforce a non-training flag and schedule deletion within 30 days after the eval unless you request otherwise. We can also restrict access to the private eval workspace to a small whitelist (PM + SE + Redwood evaluation engineer). If you want an explicit SOC2 addendum, I'll loop in our Security lead.

- Baseline on performance: based on similar legal extraction workloads we’ve run, Llama-2-Chat-13B (q4_0) is the best starting point for accuracy and should be closest to your 0.92 F1 target on seeded clause extraction when prompts are well-structured. The rw-opt-7b-int8 option typically trades 3–6 points of F1 for a ~2.5x latency improvement and lower token cost; rw-safety-7b prioritizes conservative outputs and may reduce false positives on redaction.

Proposed immediate steps (short):
1) You share 100 sanitized prompts + 15 edge cases (CSV). Use the attached template — key columns: prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_output, priority, notes. For any rows with redacted PHI include a note like "email_REDACTED:type=email".
2) We run a small seeded eval against the three model variants and return: per-prompt outputs, precision/recall/F1, median latency, and per-token cost estimate.
3) We document recommended prompt refactors and a candidate configuration (quantization + batching) you can promote to staging.

Example redaction guidance to include with your CSV: replace full names, emails, SSNs with fixed tags (NAME_REDACTED / EMAIL_REDACTED / SSN_REDACTED). Keep punctuation intact where possible to preserve tokenization. For OCR-noisy content, provide an extra column "ocr_confidence" if available.

I’ll run the eval and have a short deliverable ready within 48 hours of your upload. If you prefer we run the evaluation in your VPC, please let me know and we’ll schedule the private ingest.

Looping in Marissa (solutions engineering) to flag any prompt-refactor patterns we should apply automatically.

—
Soojin
